macro.text: Thursday: Nasdaq −5.5% (correction), S&P −4.4%, Dow −1,800+ (−3.4%), worst since Apr 2025, on fears the Democratic sweep slows data center building. Nasdaq-100 futures +1.6%, Dow −0.9%.
Asia followed: Japan's biggest one-day fall since 'liberation day', SK Hynix −11.7%, Taiwan −8%+; South Korea and Taiwan stepped in to prop up their markets.
Oil flat (WTI 90.66, Brent 98.19) but set for a sharp weekly fall from Brent above $110 Monday, on hopes for an Iran deal; three more tanker attacks in Hormuz Thursday.
Fed: December 9 hike odds about 70% (CME FedWatch), down from ~83% before Thursday. Payrolls 8:30 (59–65K expected, unemployment 4.2%).
Money hid in Treasuries Thursday: 10-yr closed 4.837% (−5.7 bp), 30-yr 5.251%; dollar index 102.06 (+0.5%); gold 4,068.90 (−1.1%).
AI credit worry: ING is shopping about $500M of data center loans, including a piece of the New Mexico Stargate project; bids due Nov 19.

flowNote: Money is coming back into the groups sold hardest: semiconductors (SMH +5.0% premarket after −11.2% Thursday and −20.3% over 5 days), tech (XLK +2.5%) and high-growth tech (ARKK +1.8%), helped by Lam's $25B buyback, plus AI power names on Vistra's raised guide (VRT +7.4%, PWR +5.6%, ETN +4.9%). It is being taken out of Thursday's relative hiding places: staples (XLP −1.8%), health care (XLV −1.5%), materials (XLB −1.2%), financials (XLF −1.0%) and real estate (XLRE −1.0%). Read it as a relief bounce, not a new trend: SMH is still −26% over a month.

Defensives fund the bounce: XLP −1.8%, XLV −1.5%, XLF −1.0%; Dow futures −0.9%

bigPicture: The market is now punishing the whole AI build-out, not just suppliers with weak guides: the Democratic sweep turned local data center limits into a national policy risk (SMH −20% in 5 days).
Thursday's selling was broad and went into Treasuries, not into defensives; today's bounce is concentrated in what fell most, with staples, health care and banks sold to pay for it.
Companies with their own good numbers still get paid (NET, ABNB, VST), and misses get hit hard (DKNG, AXON, TEAM).
Rates still cap any rebound: payrolls today, CPI Nov 10, and a December 9 hike still ~70% priced.
snapshot.takeaway: This is a relief bounce on the day after a crash, with payrolls landing before the open. Thursday's early bounce failed, so let the chip gaps show whether they hold their premarket ranges in the first 15 minutes, and favor names with their own news (NET, ABNB, VST) over sympathy gaps.

sectors.text: SMH +5.0% premarket after −11.2% Thursday (worst since March 2020) and −20.3% over 5 days. LRCX +11.4% on a $25B buyback, MU and AMD +7.8%, TSM +6.9%, AVGO +5.0%, NVDA +4.4%. No new demand numbers: it is a bounce, and Asia's chip stocks crashed overnight.

Vistra raised its 2026 EBITDA guide ($7.1–7.5B) and gave a 2027 range of $7.7–8.5B, lifting power and cooling: VRT +7.4%, PWR +5.6%, ETN +4.9%, NRG +3.0%, GEV +2.6%, CEG +2.4%. All are still 15–22% below their 20-day averages.

The spenders are not bouncing: MSFT −0.9%, AMZN, GOOGL and META flat, as the sweep raises data center permitting risk and ING shops $500M of data center loans. ORCL +3.5%; Alphabet disclosed a $548M Qualcomm stake.
Usage-based platforms beat and raise (NET +19.2%, JFrog +23% on a raised guide); seat-based names cut (TEAM −15.5%, Five9 −17%). IGV +0.9% premarket, −8.3% over 5 days.
Flat premarket (WTI 90.66, Brent 98.19) but Brent is down from above $110 Monday on Iran deal hopes; XLE −10.3% over 5 days. EOG beat and raised its dividend 8% but is only +0.2%.
